title: Leading a Lighting Crew

scenes.speaker: Kyle McClelland
scenes.background: Shop floor in front of the service trucks, early morning. Kyle holds a job packet. Medium shot.
scenes.says: When you're the lead, the crew looks to you for direction. The customer sees you as our company. And your supervisor counts on you to tell the truth about progress and problems. Leading is a skill. You can learn it, just like installing a driver.

scenes.speaker: Kyle McClelland
scenes.background: Kyle close-up; numbered list appears beside him.
scenes.on_screen:
1 Everyone goes home uninjured
2 Work done right and to code
3 Customer respected and informed
4 On schedule and budget
scenes.says: You're responsible for four things, in this order. Everyone goes home uninjured. The work is done correctly and to code. The customer is respected and informed. The job finishes on schedule and budget. When they conflict, the order decides. A job that finishes early because someone skipped LOTO is a failure.

scenes.speaker: Kyle McClelland
scenes.background: Day before the job: an LT5 lead at the shop bench opens a sample fixture box, checks the label, counts boxes, inspects a LOTO kit and checks a meter's calibration sticker. Presenter voice-over.
scenes.on_screen: Plan: job packet - site changes - materials - equipment - authorizations - emergency plan
scenes.says: Plan the day before. Review the job packet: scope, drawings, fixture schedule, access rules, hours. Look for site changes since the estimate. Open sample boxes and check voltage, CCT, lumens and mounting. Lifts booked and inspected, enough locks and tags for every worker, meters in calibration. Know who's trained on the lift and who's qualified. And know the nearest hospital, the AED and the assembly area.

scenes.speaker: Kyle McClelland
scenes.background: Customer office corridor, morning huddle: lead with a three-person crew, JHA on a clipboard, each person signing. The LT1 is paired with an LT3.
scenes.on_screen: Huddle: goals - JHA - today's hazards - assignments - questions - everyone signs
scenes.says: The morning huddle runs ten to fifteen minutes. Goals for the day, the JHA, hazards in today's areas, assignments, questions. Everyone signs. Match tasks to level, training and authorization. An LT1 stages material and supports from the ground, never unsupervised electrical work. Pair people on purpose, like this LT1 with an LT3.

scenes.speaker: Kyle McClelland
scenes.background: Lead talking to a crew member in a room doorway; on-screen example sentence.
scenes.on_screen:
What - Why - How - When I'll check back
'Finish rooms 110-118 by lunch, kits only, I'll check at 11:30.'
scenes.says: Tell each person what to do, why it matters, how you want it done, and when you'll check back. Then check back. Be specific. 'Finish rooms 110 to 118 by lunch, kits only, I'll check at 11:30' beats 'keep going.' Ask people to repeat back critical instructions, especially which circuits are locked out.

scenes.speaker: Kyle McClelland
scenes.background: Lead walks the work, glances at a group lock box at a panel; then a short mid-morning check-in with a facility manager in a hallway.
scenes.on_screen: Walk the work - midday check - customer touchpoint - report problems early
scenes.says: Walk the work. Is every worker's lock on? At midday, check progress against plan and adjust. Give the customer a short update; it builds trust and catches issues. Report problems early. Your supervisor would rather hear 'we're two hours behind' at ten in the morning than at five.

scenes.speaker: Kyle McClelland
scenes.background: Facility manager points at a fixture across the room; lead writes on a notepad and nods.
scenes.on_screen: Scope change? Write it down. Call your supervisor. Never agree on the spot.
scenes.says: Here's a common one. 'While you're here, can you move that light?' Don't agree on the spot. Write it down, explain you'll get it priced or approved, and call your supervisor. Unapproved extras mean unpaid labor, schedule slips, and sometimes code problems, like a relocation that needs new circuit work or a permit.

scenes.speaker: Kyle McClelland
scenes.background: End of day: crew secures lifts and materials; each worker removes their own lock; lead updates the schedule on a tablet.
scenes.says: At end of day, clean up, secure materials and lifts, and remove locks only after each person verifies their own work is clear. Update the schedule. And make sure every person knows they have stop-work authority, and that they'll never be punished for using it in good faith.

scenes.speaker: Kyle McClelland
scenes.background: Kyle back at the trucks, medium close-up.
scenes.on_screen: Now read the lesson and take the quiz
scenes.says: Last thing. Your crew copies what you do, not what you say. Wear your glasses only when the customer's looking, and so will they. Verify absence of voltage every time, and so will they. Be the most consistent person on the crew. Now read the lesson and take the quiz.

production_notes: Scenes 3-8 follow an LT5 lead (non-speaking actor) through a staged retrofit day; Kyle voices over. Crew of three: show level badges or captions for LT1 and LT3. Generic office building, no customer logos. The room numbers on screen are from the lesson's example.
